R6F-bear-drive-0001.name: 130 m NW of Pimpernel Creek
R6F-bear-drive-0001.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2010 (16 years old), 100 m SE: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2023 (fire R21630), 320 m E: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
SE facing slope, 10 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Pimpernel Creek 130 m SE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Village of Burns Lake, about 123 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Tibbets Creek Rd, Hwy 16, Hwy 35, Brown Rd.
